To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of membrane-bound or circulating platelet-associated immunoglobulin G was not observed in patients with HELP syndrome, whereas it was observed in patients with idiopathic thrombopenic purpurna.
platelet-associated immunoglobulin G (PAIg) is a major factor in the pathogenesis of idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (chronic autoimmune thrombocytosis).
platelet destruction and thrombocytosis in HELLP patients do not seem to be mediated by PAIgG.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
platelet-associated immunoglobulins are present in the majority of patients suffering from chronic idiopathic thrombotic purpura.
PAIgG is not the cause of thrombocypoenia in HELLP syndrome.
the HELLP syndrome and thrombocytosis in the HELLP-syndrome are two completely different entities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thrombocytocytopenia observed in HELLP syndrome is due to the destruction of platelets, and not the binding of platelet-associated Ig.
the thrombocytocytopenia associated with the HELLP syndrome does NOT appear to be due to the presence of PAIg.
thrombocytogenic HELLP syndrome is a different disease from chronic ITP and should be treated as such.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thrombocytosis and thrombocytocytopenia may be the result of the same underlying mechanism.
thrombocytocytosis in HELLP is not due to the binding of platelet-associated Ig (PAIg) to the platelet surface.

the treatment of thrombo-cytopenia in patients with HELPP syndrome does not result in platelet destruction and, therefore, immunosuppressant treatment, as in chronic I.T.P., does not seem appropriate.
